description: React components that are prerendered on the server and then hydrated on the client. Required for interactivity, browser APIs, and stateful logic. Declared with the 'use client' directive. Establish a client module graph boundary — all imports within that graph are bundled for the client.
constraints: 'use client' directive must appear at the top of the file, before any imports
All modules imported by a Client Component are included in the client JavaScript bundle
Cannot import Server Components directly — Server Components can only be passed as props (children pattern)
Cannot use async/await directly in Client Component body for data fetching — use use() API or client-side data libraries
Cannot access server-only resources (database, file system, secrets) directly
Props received from Server Components must be serializable
React context works in Client Components but not in Server Components
Environment variables without NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix are replaced with empty string — not available at runtime
allowedPatterns: useState, useReducer, useContext, useRef, useEffect, useLayoutEffect and all React client hooks
Browser APIs: window, document, localStorage, sessionStorage, navigator, IntersectionObserver, etc.
Event handlers: onClick, onChange, onSubmit, onFocus, onBlur, etc.
Custom hooks that use any of the above
Rendering Server Components passed as children or other props
Streaming data from server using React use() API with a promise passed from a Server Component
Client-side data fetching with SWR, React Query, or fetch()
Third-party packages that use client-only APIs
Wrapping third-party components that lack 'use client' to make them usable in Server Components
Lazy loading with React.lazy() and Suspense
Using useRouter, usePathname, useSearchParams, useParams navigation hooks
forbiddenPatterns: Direct database queries or ORM calls
Importing server-only modules — build error if server-only package is used
Accessing process.env variables without NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix — silently replaced with empty string
Importing a Server Component directly (breaks the server/client module graph boundary)
Using async/await at the top level of a Client Component function body
Expecting server-side secrets passed as props to remain secret — props are serialized into the page
runtimeBehavior: Prerendered on the server into HTML on first request — provides non-interactive initial preview
Hydrated on the client — JavaScript attaches event handlers and makes the component interactive
On subsequent client-side navigations: rendered entirely on the client without server involvement
RSC Payload contains placeholders for Client Components plus references to their JS file chunks
Client Component JS files are downloaded, parsed, and executed during hydration
'use client' boundary causes all transitive imports in that file's module graph to be included in the client bundle
Server Components passed as children/props are rendered on the server BEFORE being passed — they are not re-rendered on the client
Hydration must produce identical output to server-rendered HTML — mismatches cause hydration errors
useSearchParams must be wrapped in Suspense when used in Client Components to avoid blocking prerendering
architectureImplications: 'use client' is a module graph boundary declaration, not a per-component annotation — it affects all imports
Push 'use client' as far down the component tree as possible to minimize client bundle size
Context providers must be Client Components — they should wrap only the subtree that requires context
Third-party components using client APIs without 'use client' must be re-exported from a wrapper Client Component
Server Components can be passed into Client Components as props — they remain server-rendered
Client Component module graph is separate from Server Component module graph — a module imported in both contexts may be bundled twice
Prop drilling of server data into deeply nested Client Components creates coupling — prefer passing Server Components as children instead
performanceImplications: Every import in a Client Component's module graph contributes to the client JavaScript bundle
Marking large layout components as Client Components forces all children into the client bundle
Tree-shaking only removes unused exports — large client-side dependencies cannot be avoided once imported in client graph
Hydration cost is proportional to the number and complexity of Client Components in the initial render
useSearchParams without Suspense wrapper causes the entire route to opt out of static prerendering
Deferring hydration with lazy() can reduce Time to Interactive for non-critical interactive components
Client-side data fetching with SWR/React Query introduces additional network waterfalls after initial HTML load
commonMisusePatterns: Adding 'use client' to a file that doesn't need it — pulls all its imports into the client bundle unnecessarily
Placing 'use client' on a layout that is mostly static — forces all descendant components into client bundle
Importing heavy libraries (charting, editors, etc.) inside a Client Component without lazy loading
Fetching data in Client Components when a Server Component could fetch it without the client-server roundtrip
Not wrapping useSearchParams in Suspense — causes static prerender of the route to fail silently
Creating context providers as Server Components — context is client-only
Using process.env.SECRET in a Client Component — silently resolves to empty string, breaking functionality without error
productionRisks: Bundle bloat: unrestricted 'use client' propagation can include large server-only libraries in the client bundle
Hydration mismatch errors: dynamic values (Date.now(), Math.random(), browser-specific data) that differ between server prerender and client hydration cause React warnings and potential UI corruption
Silent env var failure: non-NEXT_PUBLIC_ env vars silently become empty strings in Client Components — auth tokens, API keys, and config values break without throwing
Prop serialization errors: passing non-serializable values (functions, Maps, Sets, class instances) from Server to Client Components causes runtime errors
useSearchParams without Suspense degrades static prerendering to dynamic rendering for the entire route
Context re-renders: broad context providers that wrap large subtrees cause unnecessary re-renders on any state change
